summary: A parent with a three-year-old daughter who understands Chinese is seeking childcare options while working full-time. The parent is looking for a daycare center that offers Chinese-speaking services or at least some language support. The advisor directs the parent to the website spo.fi and explains the options available, including daycare centers, which are the most common form of early childhood education. The advisor notes that while there are no Chinese-speaking daycare centers, some Finnish-speaking centers offer bilingual programs or language support. The next step is for the parent to explore these options on the website.

questionnaire.Contents of the customer visit: Family life (eg.: children's school, early childhood education, relationships)
questionnaire.Any Additional Information: The customer is looking for a daycare center in Espoo, Finland, that offers English or Mandarin-speaking services for their three-year-old daughter, as they cannot take her to work every day and are concerned about language barriers. They are also interested in understanding the costs, potential government support, and the availability of private daycare options.
questionnaire.Any other Feedback: The advisor noted that finding a Chinese-speaking daycare might be difficult and suggested looking for English-speaking options, mentioned the potential high cost of private daycare, and advised checking the website and contacting daycare centers directly for more information.
